chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: The trombone solo book and Leeds buying music
summary: His small trombone solo book is published by Mills; Leeds was buying up black and white music in the late 1930s.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yes. There's a book - you saw the trombone book in there.
No, I didn't see the trombone book. I want to see it. Trombone Book of Jay C. Higginbotham Solos, published by - ?
So that he just like had the whole field like W. C. Handy, Duke Ellington, and everybody belonged to Mills.
Oh, Leeds, yes Leeds, I apologize.
Was Leeds buying up music, black musicians' music.
Black or white music. I know they was buying it.
This? I don't know. Dates on it.
In the 30's. We were working out with Lou Armstrong. We were working down in the Cotton Club when that happened - '39.
